subject: AWS Offer: trial CTA & entitlement copy pass
messages:
From: Alice Tan <alice@cloudbridge.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: AWS offer setup — trial CTA and entitlement questions

Hi Vivek,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our product and procurement teams started the AWS offer intake and flagged two areas we need help with before we go live:

1) Trial CTA wording — procurement wants a brief, unambiguous CTA that aligns to our trial mechanics (30-day free trial with usage cap). They asked for one-line and short-paragraph variants.
2) SKU / entitlement mapping — we currently plan a single SKU with trial vs paid entitlements, but AWS marketplace may prefer distinct SKUs or footnotes to clarify billing. See the attached spreadsheet for our proposed mapping.

Can Redwood review recommended copy and confirm whether the SKU mapping will cause any listing or billing issues? We want to avoid manual procurement questions once the offer is submitted.

If possible, could Kimberly and Marissa weigh in on the microcopy and the entitlement footnote language? Were targeting a submission by 3/23.

Thanks,

Alice Tan
Head of Platform Partnerships
CloudBridge Solutions

Attachments: cloudbridge_trial-sku-map.xlsx

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Tan <alice@cloudbridge.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Mar 2028 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: AWS offer setup — trial CTA and entitlement questions

Hi Alice — great to see this moving. Quick read of the attached workbook looks sensible; two areas below are high-impact and easy to fix before submission:

- Trial CTA: keep the primary CTA short and explicit. Suggest: "Start 30‑day free trial (usage limits apply)" as the one-line. For the paragraph, a 1–2 sentence explanation that includes the cap (e.g., 100k tokens) and auto-convert behavior if applicable.

- SKUs & entitlements: AWS catalog teams often prefer a clear billing unit for paid usage. If your trial is metered and then auto-converts, we recommend: (a) a single paid SKU with an explicit trial footnote that explains conversion, OR (b) two SKUs ("Trial SKU" + "Production SKU") if you want clear differentiation in AWS billing reports. Both are valid; option (a) keeps the listing simpler.

Kimberly / Marissa: can you pull a suggested footnote and two CTA variants into the shared Drive doc? Ill confirm with our ops team whether option (a) will need any additional entitlements in the offer submission.

Ive attached a short doc with CTA variants for quick copy review.

— Vivek
Director, Partner GTM | Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Alice Tan <alice@cloudbridge.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Mar 2028 10:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: AWS offer setup — trial CTA and entitlement questions

Thanks Vivek / Alice — I did a quick pass and added the following copy snippets to the Drive link (https://drive.redwood.com/shared/cloudbridge/trial-copy-v1). Paste here for visibility:

One-line CTAs (short):
- "Start 30‑day free trial (usage limits apply)"
- "Try CloudBridge free for 30 days — limited usage included"

Short paragraph options (concise, procurement-friendly):
- "Start a 30‑day trial of CloudBridge. The trial includes up to 100k tokens of usage; after the trial ends, your account will not be charged without explicit agreement. See billing details in the product entitlements below."
- "Begin a 30‑day trial capped at 100k tokens. No automatic charges will occur unless you enable auto-conversion in your account settings."

Suggested entitlement footnote (short):
- "Trial: limited to 100k tokens. Post-trial: usage requires a paid subscription; customers will be prompted to accept terms before charges begin."

Notes / asks:
- If CloudBridge prefers the single-SKU model, add a short FAQ line in the listing to explain conversion and who initiates billing to reduce procurement questions.
- Marissa: I left two CTA variants in the Drive doc marked A/B for field testing in seller console.

Kimberly Park
Marketplace & GTM Ops

From: Alice Tan <alice@cloudbridge.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Mar 2028 15:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: AWS offer setup — trial CTA and entitlement questions

Hi Kimberly / Vivek — this is super helpful, thanks. We reviewed the CTA variants with procurement and they prefer the one-line: "Start 30‑day free trial (usage limits apply)" plus the short footnote language you suggested.

Next steps from our side: well update the workbook with the final SKU selection (likely single paid SKU + trial footnote) and route for internal legal sign-off. Can Marissa share the copy variant file (cta_variants_v1.docx) in the Drive folder and well mark which variant we want in the console?

Appreciate the quick turn — aiming to submit the offer by end of day 3/23.

Best,
Alice

\nThread notes: many short replies expected during listing submission; procurement often asks for exact token caps and a sample invoice line. Keep internal CCs limited to ops and marketplace owners to avoid noisy threads.
